title: The Flood
summary: God judges the world by a global Flood; Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives, and the animals are preserved in the Ark.
description: Genesis 6–8. The Flood begins in Noah's 600th year, 2nd month, 17th day (Gen 7:11); the earth is dry in his 601st year, 2nd month, 27th day (Gen 8:14).

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 4: Dating Creation and the Deluge," ARJ 16 (2023): 475–489, section "AP-29: The Flood: 2348–2347 B.C."
chronologies.note: Five triangulations; also CFAH-1 Introduction ("the Flood in 2348/2347 BC") and Table 1 ("2348 Flood of Noah").

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 1: Problem, Data, and Methodology," ARJ 15 (2022): 377–390, section "Our Assumptions (Declared Biases)", Table 1 "Biblically derived dates from Ussher and Jones"
chronologies.note: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones biblical baseline adopted by CFAH); not a triangulated anchor point.

chronologies.citation: Floyd Nolen Jones, Chart No. 1 "Creation to Jesus Christ" (© 1993), line "1656 AM 2348 BC the year of the FLOOD"; also Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), Chart One §B, p. 26 ("1921 + 427 = 2348 BC (year of the Flood)")
chronologies.note: Jones: Flood AM 1656 = 2348 BC (Ussher heads AM 1656 as 2349 BC).

chronologies.date: Noah's 600th year, 2nd month, 17th day (begins); 601st year, 2nd month, 27th day (earth dry)
1656 AM, 2365 JP, 2349 BC; enters Ark Sunday 7 December (Julian)
chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §34–35
chronologies.note: Ussher's heading for AM 1656 reads 2349 BC; the exit from the Ark (AM 1657) is headed 2348 BC (Second Age §40–41). "Flood 2348 BC" in popular summaries therefore conflates the two AM years.

chronologies.date: AM 1656: announcement 2/10/1656, judgment commenced 2/17/1656 (Gen 7:10-11); "1657 - End of Flood"
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 2)," Biblical Chronology 6:4 (April 1994), §4 year list ("1656 - The Flood; Methuselah died") and §5 "The Chronology of the Flood Year"
chronologies.note: Jordan writes dates as month/day/year AM. A Summary of OT Chronology (BC 4:8) §1: "This puts the Flood in the year Anno Mundi (year of the world) 1656"

chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), chart "Anno Mundi / B.C. (SBC) / B.C. (CCC)" at the start of the article
chronologies.note: B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years.

chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 11, chart table "Biblical History According To A.M & B.C. Dates"
chronologies.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 1656. The compilation's B.C. year (2354) is AM subtracted from 4010 (its own convention: Creation 4010 B.C.); Jordan's own SBC B.C. figures differ (here 2274 B.C.). Display only; never converted or used for sorting.
Methuselah (born AM 687, lived 969) dies AM 1656, the Flood year.
Josephus's received text gives 2656; Whiston inserts [one thousand six hundred and fifty-six] in brackets.

chronologies.date: "in the 600 yeare of Noeh's age came the flood" - first age, Adam to the Flood, 1656 years ("according to the 70 Interpreters" 2242)
chronologies.citation: Annals of Clonmacnoise (trans. Mageoghagan 1627, ed. Murphy 1896), p. 12

chronologies.date: "The general flood was in the year of the world 1656"
chronologies.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (11th ed. 1736, vol. 1), Book I, ch. VII, sect. III
